blend.blend_rule: slerp of captured local rotations (shortest arc) and lerp of the hips translation over 24 frames (0.80 s, the bed layer's existing 0.8 s crossfade), smoothstep weight; captured frames continue on both sides of the window

after_blend.note: after the blend the seams are exact by construction (pose 0); what remains is the blend itself: the pose gap is crossed in n_blend frames, so the joint speeds inside the blend window are the cost

lie_to_loop.needed: same posture class (supine) but a 58 cm limb/torso configuration gap: a captured settle on the owner skeleton from the lie-down's end pose into the loop's pose, or a lie-down that ends in the loop's pose, or a sleep loop captured in the lie-down's end pose. A blend cannot bridge this.

loop_to_wake.needed: same posture class (supine) but a 82 cm limb/torso configuration gap: a captured transition from the loop's pose into the get-up's lying start, or a get-up captured from the loop's pose. A blend cannot bridge this.

placement.rule: one constant rigid placement per clip: yaw about vertical fitted by 2D Kabsch on all 65 joints, then the translation that puts the hips on the previous clip's hips at the blend start; never per frame. The vertical shift moves the loop to the lie-down's bed height, which is NOT the native mattress: the bed fit (tools/fit_bed_placement.py) decides the final height.

criteria.normalised_cost: max(pose/10 cm, velocity/50 cm/s, attitude/30 deg); <= 1 is a plausible blend
